title: The Product Photo Editing Checklist Every E-commerce Seller Should Steal
description: A step-by-step editing checklist for e-commerce product photos. Save this and use it for every new listing.

blocks.text: Consistent photos = consistent sales. But most sellers edit each photo differently, in a different mood, on a different day. The result: a storefront that looks like a chaotic yard sale.
Here's the checklist top sellers use for every single product photo. Bookmark this.
✅ Pre-Editing Checklist

□ Original file saved separately
Never edit destructively. Keep raw originals in a dedicated folder.

□ File resolution verified (2000px+ recommended)
Anything smaller and you'll regret it when marketplaces demand zoom features.

□ Photo is sharp and in focus
Blurry can't be fixed. Reshoot before wasting time editing.

□ Product clearly visible, not clipped
If parts of the product are cut off, reshoot.
✅ Background Editing Checklist

□ Background removed cleanly
Use edit-photo.com for one-click AI removal. Check edges for cleanup.

□ Consistent background across catalog
White for Amazon, brand color or transparent for other platforms.

□ No shadows from original background
Shadows imply an environment. For marketplace mains, remove them.

□ Product centered with proper padding
10-15% margin around all sides.
✅ Watermark and Branding Checklist

□ Every image is licensed and free of unauthorized supplier marks
Request clean supplier originals or shoot the product yourself; do not erase ownership marks without permission.

□ Unwanted timestamps are resolved at the source
Use an original without a burned-in date, or reshoot the item when accurate reconstruction is not possible.

□ Your own branding added subtly (optional)
Small, tasteful, not overwhelming. Corner logo max 5% of image area.
✅ Color and Light Checklist

□ White balance consistent across catalog
No mixing warm and cool tones between products.

□ Product colors accurate
The blue in the photo should match the blue in real life. Returns for "color not as shown" are conversion killers.

□ No blown-out highlights
Details in white and reflective areas should still be visible.

□ Adequate contrast
Product should pop from background without looking artificial.
✅ Composition Checklist

□ Consistent aspect ratio across catalog
Pick 1:1 (square), 4:5, or 3:4—stick with it.

□ Product at consistent scale
A ring and a chair shouldn't both fill 100% of their frames. Buyers get scale confusion.

□ Multiple angles captured
Front, side, back, detail, in-use context.
✅ Platform-Specific Requirements

□ Amazon: check the current main-image requirements
Use a pure white background where required and verify the current rules for your category before publishing.

□ Etsy: use clean and lifestyle views where they help the buyer
Use available photo slots to answer real questions about scale, detail, packaging, and context.

□ Shopify: Lifestyle context photos
Emotion sells more than isolation on Shopify.

□ Instagram/TikTok: Square + vertical versions
Never post horizontal on mobile-first platforms.
✅ Final Quality Check

□ Zoom to 100% and check edges
Fuzzy hair, jewelry chains, mesh—these are where AI sometimes leaves artifacts.

□ Preview on mobile
80%+ of shoppers browse on phones. Check how it looks small.

□ Compare against 2-3 competitor listings
Does yours look premium next to theirs? If no, revise.
✅ Publishing Checklist

□ Filenames use SKU convention
SKU12345_main.jpg, SKU12345_02.jpg, etc.

□ Alt text written for accessibility and SEO
Describe the product literally. "Blue ceramic coffee mug with white handle, 12oz."

□ Compressed for the destination without visible damage
Use the platform's current size guidance and compare image quality before choosing a fixed file-size target.
The One-Hour Weekly Habit
Every Sunday, pick 10-20 photos from your catalog. Run them through this checklist. In 3 months, your entire store will look like it was shot by a professional team.
Start your checklist workflow free at edit-photo.com.
For image rights questions, start with the license or supplier agreement and seek qualified legal advice when needed.
